beats.care: Many first-time investors will hear about this from friends. An IPO price is not a promise; shares can list below it. Never borrow to bid.
beats.what: Jio Platforms, Reliance's telecom and digital arm, will sell new shares to the public from 21 to 23 October at ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 each.
beats.why: It is valued at about ₹10.3 lakh crore, making it one of India's biggest listings ever.

cards.body: An Initial Public Offering is when a company sells shares to the public for the first time. You bid in a price band; if more people bid than shares exist, allotment is by lottery and you may get nothing.
cards.title: what is an ipo?

cards.body: Up to ₹2,500 crore is kept for Reliance shareholders who held shares on 14 Oct, and ₹500 crore for employees, who get ₹54 off per share.
Brokerages expect Jio to raise mobile tariffs in the December quarter, after the IPO. Airtel has already raised postpaid plans by ₹50.

cards.q: Would you bid in a big IPO like this?
Will the public part of the Jio IPO be fully subscribed by 23 Oct?
In a fresh-issue IPO like Jio's, who gets the money raised?
cards.why: Fresh shares are newly created, so the cash goes to the company, not to anyone selling old shares.

cover.label: Minimum bid: 12 shares at the top price

hook: India's *biggest telecom IPO* opens Wednesday. What is an IPO, really?

learn.t: All ₹30,213 crore is fresh shares, so the money goes to Jio itself; no existing owner is selling any stake.

tldr: Jio Platforms' ₹30,213 crore IPO opens for the public on 21 October, with a price band of ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 a share.
watch: Public bidding runs 21–23 Oct. Allotment is on 26 Oct, and listing is expected around 28–29 Oct.
